newsitem.title: UK: Bulgaria debt takes another knock, Russia shines.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria debt takes another knock, Russia shines.

text.p: The emerging debt market resumed its attack on Bulgaria on Thursday after a brief respite, but Russia continued to shine on hopes of more positive economic news despite worries over the troubled health of the President.
High yield Bulgarian debt prices, which had risen from the depths on belief they had fallen enough, lost favour again.
One U.S. bank trader pointed to the falling lev, worries the government would start printing money and thus chances that inflation would explode.
"People have been saying Bulgaria could default for a year. You get a good return in loads of other stuff," he said.
He was countering arguments by some analysts that the yield for Bulgarian debt is so high and the actual chance of default so remote that its recent plunge made it an attractive buy.

CS First Boston, in a market commentary, said Bulgaria would need its delayed International Monetary Fund tranche by October at the latest as the central bank will need to intervene to defend the lev.
The lev was softer this morning.
Bularian debt prices have slumped 3.56 percent in the month to date, in sharp contrast to the rest of the market, with the J.P. Morgan EMBI index up nearly three percent in the same period.
Russia has been one of the biggest gainers, despite jitters ahead of President Boris Yeltsin's impending heart operation.
One analyst said the fact the Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin had been handed some of the power in the interim, reassured the market on the question of political stability.
That has given investors more freedom to dwell on the more positive economic prospects, including a likely credit rating.
CS First Boston , however, said that the government expectations on the level and timing of the rating were too optimistic.
"An early rating will almost certainly be below investment grade, within BB-/BB+," it added.
Elsewhere, Croatia is attracting increasing interest in anticipation of its credit rating.
Croatia last week appointed Merrill Lynch and Union Bank of Switzerland as advisers in obtaining a rating for its debut Eurobond issue.

Latin debt was almost ignored in London, though Argentine FRBs ARFLC05=RR slipped on some local selling following the failure by Congress on Wednesday to vote on tax increases, which are essential to help bring down the budget deficit.
The market appeared to ignore news that the Peruvian government was considering a Brady buyback.
It was seen as confirmation of an earlier-known plan, which had irritated many in the market, to repurchase debt through a single bank.
